problem.title: Inviscid Burgers finite-time gradient blow-up
problem.canonical_statement: Consider the one-dimensional inviscid Burgers equation u_t + u u_x = 0 with smooth initial data u(x,0)=u0(x). Determine a rigorous mechanism and condition under which the classical solution develops finite-time gradient blow-up.
definitions: A classical solution is C^1 in the spacetime region under discussion.
Gradient blow-up means |u_x| becomes unbounded while u can remain bounded.
assumptions: Use either periodic data or sufficient decay when invoking spatial integral identities.
success_conditions: Identify a condition on u0' implying finite-time gradient blow-up.
Derive the singular time from the solution mechanism.
Do not confuse bounded amplitude with bounded gradient.
disallowed_shortcuts: Do not cite the standard closed-form Burgers theorem as a black box.
Do not claim that L2 energy divergence is necessary for gradient blow-up.

claims.statement: For inviscid Burgers, characteristics satisfy x(t)=xi+t*u0(xi) and u(x(t),t)=u0(xi).
claims.derivation: Along x'(t)=u, d/dt u(x(t),t)=u_t+u u_x=0, so u remains u0(xi); integrating x'=u0(xi) gives x=xi+t u0(xi).

claims.statement: Along a Burgers characteristic, w=u_x obeys w'=-w^2 and hence w(t)=w0/(1+t*w0).
claims.derivation: Differentiate u_t+u u_x=0: w_t+u w_x+w^2=0. Along x'=u this becomes w'=-w^2, whose solution is w0/(1+t w0).

claims.statement: Finite-time Burgers gradient blow-up is caused by unbounded growth of the L2 energy of u.
claims.derivation: Steepening appears to concentrate the solution, suggesting the global L2 norm must diverge before the gradient diverges.

claims.statement: If min_x u0'(x)=m<0, the classical inviscid Burgers solution develops gradient blow-up no later than T=-1/m, when the characteristic map loses invertibility.
claims.derivation: The characteristic Jacobian is 1+t*u0'(xi). The gradient formula u_x=u0'(xi)/(1+t*u0'(xi)) diverges when the denominator first vanishes, at T=-1/min u0'.

claims.statement: Conservation of the L2 norm is compatible with unbounded spatial gradients; L2 control of u alone does not control u_x.
claims.derivation: The family u_n(x)=sin(nx) has the same L2 norm on [0,2pi] for every integer n, while |u_n'(0)|=n. Thus bounded amplitude energy and large gradients are not contradictory.

claims.statement: If m=min_x u0'(x)<0, the earliest characteristic-Jacobian degeneracy occurs at T=-1/m.
claims.derivation: The Jacobian is J=1+t u0'(xi). For positive t, its earliest zero is obtained at the most negative initial derivative m, hence 1+Tm=0 and T=-1/m.

claims.statement: A Burgers characteristic with initial slope w0<0 has w(t)=w0/(1+t w0) and its gradient diverges at t=-1/w0.
claims.derivation: Solve w'=-w^2 along the characteristic. The denominator reaches zero at positive time precisely when w0<0.

objections.description: For smooth decaying/periodic inviscid Burgers solutions before shock formation, the L2 energy is conserved; gradient blow-up does not require L2 divergence.

failures.reusable_constraint: Do not infer derivative singularity from divergence of a conserved global L2 norm.
